target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and its own pipeline targeting undruggable proteins in cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurodegeneration and longevity
problem: Many disease proteins cannot be drugged by conventional inhibitors; induced proximity drugs need the right effector protein for each target, which was found by trial and error.
business_model: Biotech drug discovery platform: own pipeline plus pharma collaborations (milestones and royalties, terms not disclosed)
product_category: biotech / induced proximity drug discovery platform (OmniTAC)

founders.name: Armand Cognetta
prior_employers: Inzen Therapeutics (early employee, a Flagship Pioneering startup, now Sonata)
education: Scripps Research Institute, PhD in chemical biology, under Benjamin F. Cravatt
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-authored 19 publications and patents including foundational IP for Abide Therapeutics (acquired by Lundbeck) and Vividion Therapeutics (acquired by Bayer).

competitors.name: Kymera Therapeutics
competitors.traction_then: planned to advance candidates into the clinic the following year

technical_complexity.rationale: Discovering new proximity mechanisms and effector proteins and turning them into drug candidates is research-grade chemical biology that needs pharma-scale validation.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary platform, data and patents on effector discovery are hard to copy, but the induced proximity field is crowded and well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established degrader companies kept their own platforms; General Proximity stayed independent and signed a collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo in November 2025.

market_need_then: Investors poured money into targeted protein degradation in early 2020 (Kymera $102M and Nurix about $120M in the same month), and a 2020 Business Insider piece cited over a billion dollars invested in the field.

identity.visual_style: Lowercase, minimalist headings and dictionary-style entries for key terms

brand_strength.rationale: Clear slogan and strong site voice, but the descriptive name is generic and little press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: General Proximity was a Winter 2020 YC company that stayed in stealth for years, then emerged in January 2025 with a $16M seed led by Felicis, signed an oncology collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo in November 2025 and reported a $12M round in July 2026. The founder's prior work on Abide and Vividion IP gave strong domain fit. No exit has occurred and the story is still developing.
notes: Seed conflict: Axios reported an $8M seed in 2024-12 and one profile describes a $16M total; Pulse 2.0 and longevity.technology state $16M announced 2025-01-04; recorded $16M. The 2026 round is labelled pre-Series A by Dealroom, whose page gave no date beyond July 2026 and another profile says March 2026; stage recorded as other since the investor list differs from the company's. Dealroom says over $20M raised including grants and strategic capital; company site lists grants from ARPA-H, NCI and MBC Biolabs. Competitor sources are snippets from Xconomy (Kymera and Nurix, March 2020); pages not opened. Founded year 2019 is from longevity.technology; YC page gives no year. Crunchbase snippet says Cognetta attended the University of Virginia; page not opened so not recorded. Daiichi Sankyo collaboration date 2025-11 from a BioSpace press release snippet.
